content: {"id": "f49cf9f2-a53a-4b63-8bb7-dd31914779a9", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Our Bedrock calls are returning InternalServerError across several different models in us-east-1 over the last 30 minutes. Is this an AWS service issue or something misconfigured on our side? What we see: AWS Health shows an open Amazon Bedrock operational issue in us-east-1 that started at 14:05 UTC; InvocationServerErrors rose at 14:06 on three unrelated models (Claude Sonnet 5, Nova Lite, Llama 3); teams in two other accounts report the same; we deployed nothing in the last 24 hours. It runs in an account that isn't connected here, so answer from what I've told you.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "6ca656f1-2125-462c-a390-1ea3f2e48735", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "**This is very likely an AWS service issue, not something misconfigured on your side.** I'm going only on what you've told me, since I can't see the account.

**Why it points to AWS**
- **Health event:** an open Amazon Bedrock operational issue in us-east-1 started at 14:05 UTC. Your InvocationServerErrors rose at 14:06, one minute later.
- **Unrelated models:** Claude Sonnet 5, Nova Lite, and Llama 3 are different providers and architectures. A failure across all three points to something shared in the Bedrock runtime or regional layer, not a model-specific problem.
- **Other accounts:** two other accounts report the same errors, so the cause isn't specific to your account's IAM, quotas, or configuration.
- **No deployments:** nothing changed on your side in the last 24 hours.
- **Error class:** `InternalServerError` and the InvocationServerErrors metric are server-side (5xx) signals. Misconfiguration usually shows up as 4xx errors, such as AccessDenied, ValidationException, ResourceNotFound, or Throttling (429).

**Timing mismatch**
You said the errors started within the last 30 minutes, but it's now about 18:52 UTC and the Health event began at 14:05 UTC, nearly 5 hours ago. Either the impact has been ongoing for about 4h45m, or the errors recur in waves. Check which, because it affects how long you plan to ride this out. If your own error graphs show failures before 14:05, or a separate error pattern, that part might not be the AWS event.

**What I'd do**
- **Retries:** use exponential backoff with jitter, and make sure your SDK retry settings aren't amplifying load during the event.
- **Failover:** if your workloads allow it, route to another region, for example through cross-region inference profiles or a secondary region you've already enabled for these models. Check data-residency and model-availability constraints first.
- **Circuit breaker:** fail fast or serve a degraded response instead of queuing requests that will time out.
- **Health event:** follow its updates for mitigation status. If you have business impact, open an AWS Support case that references the Health event.

**What would change my view:** errors in your account that began before 14:05, errors only on certain IAM roles or VPC endpoints, or a mix of 4xx and 5xx codes. In that case I'd look at your side too.

If you can connect the account here, or paste a sample of the error responses and request IDs, I can dig into the specifics.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
